first.rationale: The current situation shows simultaneous declines in both activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ). Memory 31 and 86 are directly relevant: both document that simplifying/shortening onboarding improves completion and early adoption. Since we have capacity for exactly one experiment and the primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, addressing the onboarding completion decline addresses a measurable operational problem with proven precedent. This differs from promotional pricing (reactive to competition, potentially margin-eroding) and referral incentives (better suited for established customer base). Simplify_onboarding is the highest-confidence lever for recovering the 4% completion decline and likely improves activation as a secondary effect. We're verifying the two most recent onboarding-focused memories to confirm the effect size and ensure conditions remain similar. A standard_experiment scale is appropriate—we're not overcommitting with broad rollout given the QoQ decline uncertainty, but this is material enough to warrant more than a guarded test.
